subject: Post-call: Atlas Retail streaming assistant - workload & SLO clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@atlasretail.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Atlas Retail streaming assistant - workload & SLO clarifications

Samir / Lena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can size a pilot and scope SLA buckets. I summarized what we heard and flagged the items we need you to confirm.

1) Use case summary (what we discussed)
- Live shopping assistant embedded in product pages (streaming responses while agent generates).
- Typical request is a multi-turn prompt combining user context and product catalog snippets; we expect many short interactions plus some long generative responses.

2) Desired SLOs (customer stated)
- Time-to-first-token (interactive feel): p95 < 300 ms
- Per-token streaming latency: p95 < 100 ms token-to-token
- End-to-end completion for median shorter answers: ~ < 2s (for larger answers this will be longer due to generation time)

3) Workload signals we need confirmed (please fill in where I put '?' below):
- Steady-state QPS: ~ ? (you estimated low-teens)
- Peak burst QPS (5–10 minute windows): ~ ?
- Average generated tokens per response: ?
- Average prompt tokens per request: ?
- Typical concurrency (sessions that remain open while streaming): ? (or average session duration)

4) Attachments: I attached an empty workload template (atlas-workload-profile.xlsx) to capture exact event distributions. Please drop in real numbers if you have them.

Next steps / asks (short):
- Samir: fill in the items in section (3) above and share any recent traffic spikes or demo logs.
- Redwood: once we have numbers, we will return a pilot capacity estimate (tokens/sec and GPU slot sizing) and recommended model/quantization options for a canary.
- Schedule: propose a 45 min follow-up to walk numbers and pilot proposal — next Tue/Wed morning PT?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: atlas-workload-profile.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@atlasretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlasretail.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 18:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Atlas Retail streaming assistant - workload & SLO clarifications

Jordan — thanks for the clean recap. Filling in the numbers from our telemetry and the team we pulled in:

- Steady-state QPS: 12 qps (95% of the day during business hours)
- Peak burst QPS: 110 qps (observed during promo events; peaks last about 6–8 minutes)
- Average generated tokens per response: 320 tokens (we measured across pilot queries)
- Average prompt tokens per request: 140 tokens (includes product context pulls we attach)
- Typical session duration: ~14s of streaming on average (generation at ~25 tokens/sec)
- Concurrency observed at peak (rough calc): peak QPS * avg duration -> 110 * 14 ≈ 1540 concurrent streaming sessions

Other notes:
- We care about time-to-first-token mainly on product pages (mobile web); p95 < 300ms is a hard preference. For longer answers we'll tolerate longer completion times, but token streaming needs to feel snappy.
- Security/compliance: data-in-flight must be TLS; we will need SOC2 evidence and fine-grained audit logs for any pilot (I attached a short telemetry export).

I've attached a small telemetry CSV and updated a couple cells in your workbook. Happy to sync next Tue morning PT (10am PT works for us).

—Samir
Samir Kapoor
VP Product, Atlas Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Atlas Retail streaming assistant - workload & SLO clarifications

Team — copying our internal sizing/solutions folks. Quick read and proposed approach based on Samir's numbers:

1) Token math (peak vs steady) — use Samir's numbers: avg total tokens/request = 460 (320 gen + 140 prompt)
- Steady tokens/sec = 12 qps * 460 = 5,520 tokens/sec
- Peak tokens/sec = 110 qps * 460 = 50,600 tokens/sec
- Peak concurrency estimate (Samir calc) ~ 1,540 streaming sessions (matches 110 * 14s)

2) Model & runtime guidance (initial pilot)
- Recommend a streaming-optimized 7B variant (fast start time + low per-token cost). Suggest 4-bit quantized variant for pilot to reduce GPU memory and increase multiplexing.
- If Atlas requires faster time-to-first-token at peak, propose dedicated pool with continuous batching disabled for first-token paths and prefix caching for common catalog prompts.

3) Capacity sketch (rough) — our quick back-of-envelope:
- With Redwood baseline, a single instance (A100-like) can sustain ~8–10k tokens/sec for streaming-optimized 7B quantized; for 50k tokens/sec we would need ~5–6 such slots (with conservative overhead for networking and tail latency).
- Because peak windows are short (6–8m) propose reserved dedicated pool sized to handle 60% of peak, with autoscale-on-burst to cover remaining crest. That reduces committed cost but keeps the experience across spikes.

4) Security & compliance: prepare SOC2 notes and audit log sample for Samir before the follow-up. Monica, can you attach the redwood-sla-options.pdf and the SOC2 evidence excerpt?

5) Next actions (internal):
- Ben: produce a short pilot capacity estimate with 2 cost buckets — reserved-only and reserved + burst. (Due Mon COB)
- Monica: attach SOC2 evidence + retention window options. (Due Mon COB)
- Jordan: lock the follow-up time with Atlas and share the updated workbook.

I'll draft the capacity note once Ben drops the numbers. Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

If anything changes before Tue, ping me on this thread. Looking forward to getting a small pilot up quickly.

Best — Jordan
